questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼\text{Exp}(\theta )$ and unknown rate parameter $\theta .$ The log-likelihood function of the sample $5.1,\,4.2,\,6.3$ is

$$
l(\theta )=a\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +b\theta .
$$

What is the value of $a+b?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i};\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent exponential random variables with unknown parameter $\theta ,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x,\theta )=\theta {e}^{-\theta x},\,x\ge 0.
$$

Next, we write down the log-density function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡f(x,\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\theta {e}^{-\theta x}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-\theta x}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta x.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {x}_{i}) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =n\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} & =5.1+4.2+6.3=15.6\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=3.$ Therefore,  

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta -\theta \cdot 15.6 \\  & =3\operatorname{ln}⁡\theta +(-15.6)\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b=3+(-15.6)=-12.6.
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{10}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼N(\theta ,{1}^{2}),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown mean. For a particular sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{10},$ you're given that 

$$
{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}=41.2,\,{\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}^{2}=182.6.
$$

 
Given that the log-likelihood function of the sample is

$$
l(\theta )=-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )+a+b\theta +c{\theta }^{2},
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$

*Hint: The probability density function for a normal random variable with mean $\theta $ and standard deviation $1$ is given by* 

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i};\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=10$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x,\theta )=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Next, we write down the log-density function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡f(x,\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{(x-\theta )^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{n}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\frac{({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{n}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{1}{2}({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

We are told that ${\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}=41.2,$ ${\sum }_{i=1}^{10}{x}_{i}^{2}=182.6,$ and $n=10.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =-\frac{10}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{1}{2}(182.6-2\theta \cdot 41.2+10{\theta }^{2}) \\  & =-5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )+(-91.3)+41.2\theta +(-5){\theta }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=(-91.3)+41.2+(-5)=-55.1.
$$

questions.problem:
Suppose ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},{X}_{3}$ is an I.I.D random sample with ${X}_{i}∼N(\theta ,{1}^{2}),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown mean. The log-likelihood function of the sample $0.5,\,-0.8,\,-1.3$ is

$$
l(\theta )=-1.5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )+a+b\theta +c{\theta }^{2}
$$

What is the value of $a+b+c?$
questions.worked_solution:
Recall that if ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ are independent and identically distributed continuous random variables with probability density function $f(x;\theta ),$ where $\theta $ is an unknown parameter, then the log-likelihood function of a random sample ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡L(\theta ) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({\prod }_{i=1}^{n}f({x}_{i};\theta )) \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\operatorname{ln}⁡(f({x}_{i};\theta )).\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we are given a sample of $n=3$ independent normal random variables with unknown mean $\theta $ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=1,$ for which the probability density function is

$$
f(x,\theta )=\frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-\frac{1}{2}{(\frac{x-\theta }{\sigma })}^{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Next, we write down the log-density function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡f(x,\theta ) & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }}{e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi }})+\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{-(x-\theta )^{2}/2}) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{(x-\theta )^{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can calculate the log-likelihood function as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}(-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}}{2}) \\  & =-\frac{n}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}\frac{({x}_{i}-\theta )^{2}}{2} \\  & =-\frac{n}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{1}{2}({\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2}-2\theta {\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}+n{\theta }^{2})\end{aligned}
$$

For our sample, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}S & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =0.5+(-0.8)+(-1.3) \\  & =-1.6 \\ C & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =(0.5)^{2}+(-0.8)^{2}+(-1.3)^{2} \\  & =2.58\end{aligned}
$$

and $n=3.$ Therefore,  

$$
\begin{aligned}l(\theta ) & =-\frac{3}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )-\frac{1}{2}(2.58-2\theta \cdot (-1.6)+3{\theta }^{2}) \\  & =-1.5\operatorname{ln}⁡(2\pi )+(-1.29)+(-1.6)\theta +(-1.5){\theta }^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, 

$$
a+b+c=-1.29+(-1.6)+(-1.5)=-4.39.
$$
